messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Region=us-midwest (mw1) elevated 5xx and timeouts on gateway-proxy-*, breach of latency SLOs (p95 > 1.2s, 5xx rate > 4%). Auto-page to oncall.

pagerduty-sam: I'm on it. Getting context now — is this only mw1?

jules (eng-sre): seeing the same in metrics. Topology shows spike in upstream timeouts to auth-service (auth-cluster-mw1). Error pattern: mix of 502/504 from upstream and gateway 503s when backpressure kicks in.

maria (oncall): adding everyone. Customer-facing impact: some requests failing for long-running completions and sometimes short requests. CS reported an increase in tickets.

ashok (eng-runtime): logs from edge: ``[gateway] upstream request failed: UpstreamTimeoutError GET /v1/complete 504 (peer=10.12.5.4:443)``. Hit count on auth-cluster-mw1 pods is extremely high. KV cache hit ratio dropped ~30%.

pagerduty-sam: can we throttle ingest or route to another region? What's the risk?

jules (eng-sre): We can shift a fraction of traffic to us-central (uc1) by adjusting route weight in the global router. Recommend progressive shift 10% -> 30% -> 60% while we stabilize.

tanvi (netops): I can make the route change. Preparing a short window and health-check gating.

pagerduty-sam: also need to check Dedicated pools for mw1 — are any workers overloaded?

ashok (eng-runtime): Dedicated gpu pools are near capacity; autoscale didn't trigger because cluster autoscaler saw PVC limits. I'm investigating.

maria (oncall): quick customer comm: "We're investigating increased error rates for mw1. Mitigations underway, may reroute traffic to nearby regions. Will update in 10m." @customer-success-ops please amplify. :loud_sound:

customer-success-ops: posted to status page and prowling support queue. Noted spike from a handful of enterprise customers in us-midwest.

jules (eng-sre): tanvi, please run a 10% weight shift to uc1 and watch 5xx/latency. If health checks fail, roll back. Command to change weight (internal):
```
# internal router CLI
routerctl set-weight region us-midwest 0.9 us-central 0.1 --mode progressive
routerctl watch-health --route gateway-proxy
```

tanvi (netops): executing now. Will post health deltas.

incident-bot: ROUTER CHANGE: user=tanvi action=set-weight details={"us-midwest":0.9,"us-central":0.1} start_ts=3567891260

jules (eng-sre): immediate metrics: 5xx rate dropping ~15% in mw1, latency p95 improving slightly. uc1 seeing 10% traffic uptick and ok so far.

pagerduty-sam: good. while traffic shifts, can runtime team enable prefix/KV cache warmup for uc1 to avoid cold-start penalties?

ashok (eng-runtime): starting a cache-warmup job for critical prefixes and preloading common KV entries to uc1. Command: ``kubectl -n runtime exec -it job/warmup -- /bin/warmup --prefixes=common_prompts``

maria (oncall): monitoring SLOs and support chatter. Two enterprise customers still report errors intermittently but OK for most users.

jules (eng-sre): discovered root cause signals: auth-cluster-mw1 handles both auth & token-issuing for older endpoints. There is a slow regression in token handshake causing high tail latency under load. We'll isolate that service and route auth calls to uc1 token pool temporarily.

ashok (eng-runtime): we can flip auth routing by updating service map with fallback pool. Patch applied:```
# service map change
servicectl update auth-service --fallback-pool=uc1-token-pool --threshold=0.05
```

incident-bot: SERVICE MAP CHANGE: auth-service fallback set to uc1-token-pool by ashok at 3567891400

maria (oncall): auth fallback live. Watch for errors due to cross-region auth latency. Early telemetry: auth lat p95 increased from 40ms -> 120ms for routed requests but success rate much higher.

pagerduty-sam: good tradeoff. Can we also relieve mw1 by draining some noncritical worker tasks?

ashok (eng-runtime): draining low-priority batch jobs on mw1 now: ``kubectl -n workloads scalejob batch-workers --replicas=0``. That freed ~18% CPU.

jules (eng-sre): after these mitigations, overall 5xx rate in mw1 down from 4.6% -> 1.1%. Still seeing intermittent gateway 502s during small spikes. Recommend keeping route partial shift for 30m then slow-roll back to normal if stable.

maria (oncall): starting 30m mitigation window on status update. ETA next update in 15m.

customer-success-ops: added note to affected customers that mitigation is in progress and we expect service to be stable soon.

pagerduty-sam: postmortem tasks to track: root cause triage in token handshake microservice, why autoscaler didn't add nodes (PVC limitation), test fallback routing playbook. I'll own the incident write-up.

ashok (eng-runtime): follow-ups: add capacity check for PVCs in autoscaler, add CI load test for token handshake path, improve warmup heuristics for cross-region shifts.

jules (eng-sre): also recommend a temporary circuit-breaker change to reduce cascading 5xx impact: lower retry attempts and increase per-host concurrency cap for mw1 gateway-proxy. Example config snippet pushed:```
# envoy config fragment
circuit_breakers:
  thresholds:
    - priority: DEFAULT
      max_connections: 20000
      max_pending_requests: 400
      max_retries: 1
```

maria (oncall): closing the active paging loop for now — sustained metrics are within acceptable degraded bounds. Leave the routing weight at us-midwest 0.8 / us-central 0.2 for 30m to ensure full recovery. If any new spikes, re-open incident.

pagerduty-sam: thanks team. We'll keep monitoring for the next hour and collect logs for postmortem. Good triage and quick routing play. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=mitigated summary="routing shift + auth fallback + worker drain reduced 5xx and restored most traffic" mitigated_ts=3567891590

customer-success-ops: sent final update to customers: "Issue mitigated, we're investigating root cause and will post follow-up. If you continue to see errors please ping support."

jules (eng-sre): adding a note to run a controlled failover drill next week to validate our progressive route-shift automation end-to-end.

pagerduty-sam: assigning postmortem and action items in JIRA. Closing thread unless anyone needs follow-up here."
